column1: # Project filename rule: one table, three implementations (issue #23, #838).
# Every implementation of the rule that names a new project file -- src/Project.zig
# (sanitizeFilename), windows/projectname/src/lib.rs (sanitize_filename) and
# macos/Sources/Features/Projects/ProjectFilename.swift -- runs every row of this
# file in its own tests and must produce the expected column byte for byte.
# tools/every-project-filename-rule-reads-the-table.py checks that each of them
# refers to this file.
# The rule: walk the name by Unicode scalar, no normalization, not by grapheme
# cluster (the three standard libraries carry different Unicode versions, so a
# grapheme cut cannot be guaranteed to agree); replace scalars <= U+001F, U+007F,
# / \ : * ? " < > | with _; stop before the scalar that would take the result
# past 200 UTF-8 bytes; nothing left -> ERR:InvalidName; append .json.
# Columns (tab-separated): input as UTF-8 hex, expected filename as UTF-8 hex
# or ERR:InvalidName, status, note. Hex because the inputs hold control bytes,
# path separators and half-cut characters that an editor or git would change.
# status: ok    -- every implementation must match.
#         draft -- decided but not yet measured: read and counted, not
#                  asserted. (No row is draft right now; the NTFS rows were,
#                  until a Windows test measured them.)
# Every consumer asserts it read exactly `rows` data rows, so a reader that
# finds nothing fails instead of passing. Lines starting with # are comments.
# A line may end in \r (a Windows checkout); strip that and nothing else.
# Do NOT trim lines or fields: the empty-name row's input column is empty, so
# that line starts with a tab, and trimming it shifts every column left.
# Split on the tab character only.
# rows: 20
